record.title: Wormald's isomorphic linear-forest partition conjecture for cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph with an even number of edges. Equivalently, $|V(G)|$ is divisible by $4$. A **linear forest** is a forest whose components are paths, and a linear partition is a partition of the edge set into linear forests.

**Wormald's conjecture.** There exists a linear partition of $G$ into two isomorphic linear forests.

This is equivalent to a $2$-edge-colouring whose monochromatic subgraphs are isomorphic linear forests. The paper reports no counterexamples below $32$ vertices, but the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Marien Abreu, Jan Goedgebeur, Domenico Labbate and Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo, “Colourings of cubic graphs inducing isomorphic monochromatic subgraphs”, arXiv:1705.06928 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.06928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

record.title: Buratti–Sajna conjecture on resolvable directed cycle decompositions
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive odd integer. The complete symmetric digraph $K_{2m}^*$ is the digraph with both directed arcs between every pair of distinct vertices, and a **resolvable directed $m$-cycle decomposition** is a partition of its arcs into spanning subdigraphs, each a vertex-disjoint union of directed cycles of length $m$.

**Buratti–Sajna conjecture.** $K_{2m}^*$ admits a resolvable directed $m$-cycle decomposition if and only if $m\geq 5$.

This conjecture completes the determination of the odd cycle-length case of the directed Oberwolfach Problem. The cited work establishes the corresponding existence result for odd $m$ with $5\leq m\leq 49$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Andrea Burgess, Nevena Francetic and Mateja Sajna, “On the directed Oberwolfach Problem with equal cycle lengths: the odd case”, arXiv:1706.06625 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06625

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: Higher-order Turán inequality for the partition function
record.statement:
Let $p(n)$ denote the number of partitions of the positive integer $n$, and define

$$
u_n=\frac{p(n+1)p(n-1)}{p(n)^2}.
$$

**Higher-order partition-function inequality.** For $n\geq 2$,

$$
4(1-\nu_n)(1-\nu_{n+1})<\left(1+\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{24}n^{3/2}}\right)(1-\nu_n\nu_{n+1})^2.
$$

This is presented as a higher-order analogue of a conjecture of DeSalvo and Pak. The supplied text does not state that this inequality has been proved or disproved, so its resolution is unclear.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Dennis X. Q. Jia and Larry X. W. Wang, “Higher Order Turán Inequalities for the Partition Function”, arXiv:1706.10245 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.10245

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: The average Second Neighborhood Conjecture for Eulerian digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph with no loops or digons. For each vertex $v\in V(D)$, let $N^{+}(v)$ and $N^{+2}(v)$ denote its first and second out-neighborhoods, respectively. **Average Second Neighborhood Conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{v\in V(D)}|N^{+2}(v)|\geq \sum_{v\in V(D)}|N^{+}(v)|.
$$

Equivalently, the average size of the second out-neighborhood is at least the average size of the first out-neighborhood. The supplied source attributes this conjecture to Conjecture 6.15 of Sullivan and gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Michael Cary, “Vertices with the Second Neighborhood Property in Eulerian Digraphs”, arXiv:1711.01189 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.01189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: Maximal equiangular line sizes in dimensions 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20
record.statement:
Let $N(d)$ denote the maximal number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb R^d$. The proposed values are

$$
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
d & 14 & 16 & 17 & 18 & 19 & 20 \\\ \hline
N(d) & 28 & 40 & 48 & 56 & 72 & 90
\end{array}
$$

**Maximal equiangular line sizes conjecture.** The maximal numbers of equiangular lines in the specified dimensions are given by the table above.

The conjecture records the authors' proposed exact values for these extremal configurations. The paper establishes constructions, including 56 equiangular lines in $\mathbb R^{18}$, but the supplied text does not state that all six upper bounds have been proved.
record.source_name: Yen-chi Roger Lin and Wei-Hsuan Yu, “Saturated configuration and new large construction of equiangular lines”, arXiv:1801.04502 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04502

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Schmidt's conjecture on perfect binary sequences with parameter $d=1$
record.statement:
A **perfect binary sequence** is a binary periodic sequence of period $n$ with constant periodic autocorrelation at every nonzero shift; $d$ denotes this constant autocorrelation value.

**Schmidt's conjecture.** There do not exist perfect binary sequences with

$$
n>13 \quad\text{and}\quad d=1.
$$

The only known perfect binary sequences in this case have $n=5$ and $n=13$, and nonexistence is known for $13<n<20605$. The conjecture remains open beyond the established range.
record.source_name: X. Niu, H. Cao and K. Feng, “Non-existence of perfect binary sequences”, arXiv:1804.03808 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.03808

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2018). “This conjecture is still open.”

record.title: The detachable-pair classification conjecture for simple 3-connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple $3$-connected graph with $|E(G)| \ge 13$.

**Detachable-pair classification conjecture.** Either $G$ has a pair of edges $\{x,y\}$ such that either $G\backslash x\backslash y$ or $G/x/y$ is a simple $3$-connected graph; $G$ is a wheel; $G \cong K_{3,k}$ for some $k \ge 5$; $G$ is a twisted wheel; or $G$ is an unhinged multi-dimensional wheel.

This is the graphic interpretation of the preceding matroid conjecture and concerns the existence of pairs of edges whose deletion or contraction preserves simplicity and $3$-connectivity. The listed graph families are the exceptional possibilities; the conjecture is open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nick Brettell, Geoff Whittle and Alan Williams, “N-detachable pairs in 3-connected matroids III: the theorem”, arXiv:1804.06588 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06588

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: Conjecture on exclusion from the sets S^{TFFF}(n) and S^{FFFF}(n)
record.statement:
Let $S^{TFFF}(n)$ and $S^{FFFF}(n)$ be the classes of cyclically presented groups defined in the source, and let $\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)$ be the corresponding group. **Exclusion conjecture.** Let $n\geq 19$.

1. If $n\equiv 0\pmod 6$, then
 
$$
\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)\notin S^{TFFF}(n).
$$

2. If $n\equiv 2,4\pmod 6$, then
 
$$
\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)\notin S^{FFFF}(n).
$$

The conjecture is based on GAP experiments comparing abelianisations for $n\leq 500$ and is stated as an answer to whether the group can belong to the indicated classes; no proof or resolution is given.
record.source_name: Esamaldeen Mohamed and Gerald Williams, “An investigation into the cyclically presented groups with length three positive relators”, arXiv:1806.06821 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.06821

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

record.title: Schur positivity for parity-restricted initial segments
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\mu\vdash n$, and use the reverse lexicographic order on partitions of $n$. For a partition $\lambda$, let $\ell(\lambda)$ denote its number of parts, and let $p_\lambda$ be the corresponding power-sum symmetric function. **Parity-restricted initial-segment conjecture.** The sum

$$
\sum_{\substack{(1^n)\leq\lambda\leq\mu\\ n-\ell(\lambda)\ \text{even}}}p_\lambda
$$

is Schur-positive. The paper reports verification for $n\leq 20$, but leaves the assertion open for general $n$ and $\mu$.
record.source_name: Sheila Sundaram, “On a positivity conjecture in the character table of S_n”, arXiv:1808.01416 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01416

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

record.title: Chan and Mao's monotonicity conjecture for overpartition ranks
record.statement:
Let $\overline{N}(m,n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ with $D$-rank $m$, and let $\overline{N2}(m,n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ with $M_2$-rank $m$. **Chan and Mao's conjecture.** For $(m,n)\neq (0,4)$ with $n\neq |m|+2$, one has

$$
\overline{N}(m,n)\geq \overline{N}(m,n-1).
$$

For $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $n\geq 0$, one has

$$
\overline{N2}(m,n)\geq \overline{N2}(m,n-1).
$$

These inequalities assert monotonicity in the size parameter for the two overpartition rank distributions, with the stated exception and restriction for the $D$-rank inequality. The conjecture was proposed by Chan and Mao in 2014; its resolution status is not established by the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Huan Xiong and Wenston J. T. Zang, “Monotonicity properties for ranks of overpartitions”, arXiv:1808.04282 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.04282

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for stack-sorting preimages of increasing-pattern classes
record.statement:
For an integer $m\geq 2$ and $1\leq n\leq 2^{m-1}-1$, let $\operatorname{Av}_n(123\cdots m)$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ avoiding the increasing pattern $123\cdots m$, and let $s$ denote the stack-sorting map. **Unimodality conjecture.** For each integer $m\geq 2$, the sequence

$$
\bigl(|s^{-1}(\operatorname{Av}_n(123\cdots m))|\bigr)_{n=1}^{2^{m-1}-1}
$$

is unimodal. The restriction to these initial terms is natural because the corresponding preimage set is empty for $n\geq 2^{m-1}$.
record.source_name: Colin Defant, “Stack-Sorting Preimages of Permutation Classes”, arXiv:1809.03123 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03123

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

record.title: The n=8 maximal-vertex neighborhood conjecture
record.statement: Consider the vertex graph for the blind-decoding objective at matrix size $n=8$, and call a vertex **maximal** when it corresponds to a globally maximal objective value. Each vertex has 64 neighbors. **The $n=8$ maximal-vertex neighborhood conjecture.** For $n=8$, maximal vertices are the only vertices such that the objective function decreases by a factor of $0.25$ at every one of their 64 neighbors. The condition is necessary for maximal vertices; the paper reports that no non-maximal examples were found, but defers a rigorous proof of sufficiency.
record.source_name: Thomas Dean, Jonathan Perlstein, Mary Wootters and Andrea Goldsmith, “Fast Blind MIMO Decoding through Vertex Hopping”, arXiv:1810.07856 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.07856

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

record.title: Polynomial formulas for signed pancake stacks requiring five to nine flips
record.statement:
Let $R_k^B(n)$ denote the number of signed permutations of size $n$ whose burnt-pancake distance from the sorted stack is $k$. **Polynomial formulas conjecture.** If $n\geq1$, then

$$
R^B_5(n)=\frac{1}{6}n(n-1)(n-2)(6n^2-17n+3),
$$

$$
R^B_6(n)=\frac{1}{60}n(n-1)(n-2)(60n^3-343n^2+401n+284),
$$

$$
R^B_7(n)=\frac{1}{240}n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(240n^3-1499n^2+925n+5104),
$$

$$
R^B_8(n)=\frac{1}{5040}n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(5040n^4-52123n^3+113415n^2+314716n-1027242),
$$

and

$$
R^B_9(n)=\frac{1}{40320}(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n-4)(40320n^5-444061n^4+644746n^3+6638777n^2-18991470n).
$$

These formulas were obtained by polynomial fitting and also explain the zero entries in the cited data table; the source provides no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Saúl A. Blanco, Charles Buehrle and Akshay Patidar, “On the number of pancake stacks requiring four flips to be sorted”, arXiv:1902.04055 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

record.title: Ji–Zhang–Zhao inequalities for overpartition ranks
record.statement:
Let $\overline N(a,c,n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ whose rank is congruent to $a$ modulo $c$.

**Ji–Zhang–Zhao inequalities.** For $n\geq 0$ and $1\leq i\leq 4$,

$$
\overline N(0,10,5n+i)+\overline N(1,10,5n+i)\geq \overline N(4,10,5n+i)+\overline N(5,10,5n+i).
$$

For $n\geq 0$,

$$
\overline N(1,10,n)+\overline N(2,10,n)\geq \overline N(3,10,n)+\overline N(4,10,n).
$$

These inequalities concern the relative sizes of residue classes of overpartition ranks. The paper states them as conjectures of Ji, Zhang and Zhao and Wei and Zhang; its abstract says that the inequalities are proved for $n=6$ and $n=10$, while the general assertions remain open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Alexandru Ciolan, “Ranks of overpartitions: Asymptotics and inequalities”, arXiv:1904.07055 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Wei–Zhang inequalities for overpartition ranks modulo 6
record.statement:
Let $\overline N(a,c,n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ whose rank is congruent to $a$ modulo $c$.

**Wei–Zhang inequalities.** For $n\geq 11$,

$$
\overline N(0,6,3n)\geq \overline N(1,6,3n)=\overline N(3,6,3n)\geq \overline N(2,6,3n),
$$

$$
\overline N(0,6,3n+1)\geq \overline N(1,6,3n+1)=\overline N(3,6,3n+1)\geq \overline N(2,6,3n+1),
$$

and

$$
\overline N(1,6,3n+2)\geq \overline N(2,6,3n+2)\geq \overline N(0,6,3n+2)\geq \overline N(3,6,3n+2).
$$

These are inequalities among overpartition rank classes in residue classes modulo $6$. The supplied text attributes them to Wei and Zhang and gives no resolution evidence, so their general status is left open.
record.source_name: Alexandru Ciolan, “Ranks of overpartitions: Asymptotics and inequalities”, arXiv:1904.07055 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07055

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Lin's conjecture on a cubic partition-pair congruence modulo 81
record.statement:
Let $b(n)$ denote the cubic partition-pair function defined by

$$
\sum\limits_{n\geq 0}b(n)q^n=\frac{1}{f_1^2f_2^2},
$$

where $f_k=(q^k;q^k)_\infty$. **Lin's conjecture.** For each $n\geq 0$,

$$
b(81n+61)\equiv 0\pmod{81}.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the known congruence $b(81n+61)\equiv0\pmod{27}$ and concerns Ramanujan-type congruences for cubic partition pairs. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: D. S. Gireesh, M. S. Mahadeva Naika and Shivashankar C, “On 3 and 9-regular cubic partitions”, arXiv:1907.00674 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00674

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: The Hepp-bound faithfulness conjecture for primitive phi-four graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph that is p-logarithmic in $d=4$ dimensions and whose vertices all have degree at most $4$; call such a graph a $\phi^4$ graph. Let $\mathcal{P}(G)$ denote its period and $\mathcal{H}(G)$ its Hepp bound. **Hepp-bound faithfulness conjecture.** Two $\phi^4$ graphs have equal periods if and only if they have equal Hepp bounds. The conjecture is supported by computations for primitive $\phi^4$ graphs through $11$ loops, but remains open; it is motivated by analogous conjectures for the $c_2$ invariant and the permanent.
record.source_name: Erik Panzer, “Hepp's bound for Feynman graphs and matroids”, arXiv:1908.09820 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1704.06350](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06350).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.09820

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

record.title: The planar signed-graph characterization by four girth conditions
record.statement: Let $(G,\sigma)$ be a planar signed graph. For $ij\in\{00,01,10,11\}$, let $g_{ij}(G,\sigma)$ be the shortest length of a closed walk of type $ij$, and let $\operatorname{SPC}(k)$ be the signed projective cube of dimension $k$. **The planar signed-graph characterization conjecture.** The signed graph $(G,\sigma)$ maps to $\operatorname{SPC}(k)$ if and only if the four girth conditions in the no-homomorphism lemma are satisfied. This is presented as a uniform restatement of the signed projective cube conjecture; the source records verification only for the cases $k\leq 7$, leaving the general characterization open.
record.source_name: Reza Naserasr, Eric Sopena and Thomas Zaslavsky, “Homomorphisms of signed graphs: An update”, arXiv:1909.05982 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05982

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2019). “This conjecture has recently been disproved in .”

record.title: Distinct-part bound conjecture for the missing-integer parity difference
record.statement:
Let $P(n,m)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ with $m$ missing integers, and define

$$
\mathcal{M}_e(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \rfloor}P(n,2k),\qquad \mathcal{M}_o(n)=\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor}P(n,2k-1).
$$

Let $q(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. **Distinct-part bound conjecture.** For $n>10$,

$$
\mathcal{M}_e(n)-\mathcal{M}_o(n)<q(n).
$$

The conjecture gives an upper bound for the parity difference in terms of distinct-part partitions. The source offers no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Subhash Chand Bhoria, Pramod Eyyunni and Subhrangsu Santra, “On the number of missing integers in partitions”, arXiv:2604.12557 (2026).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1911.11038](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11038).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12557

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

record.title: Conjecture on equiangular lines saturating the relative and incoherence bounds
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a set of equiangular lines in $\mathbf{R}^d$ that saturates the relative bound and incoherence bound.

**Classification conjecture.** Then $d=2,3,6,7,23$, and $\Omega$ is isometric to the corresponding example found in the examples section.

The conjecture proposes that the known examples exhaust the equiangular-line sets simultaneously attaining these bounds. It is presented after a theorem giving structural restrictions for such sets; the supplied text does not establish the classification.
record.source_name: Neil I. Gillespie, “Equiangular lines, Incoherent sets and Quasi-symmetric designs”, arXiv:1809.05739 (2018).
